dedupe_keys.name: kosice region landscape and watershed restoration programme for water retention slovakia

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Košice Region Landscape Restoration Programme in south-east Slovakia, a region of 6,754 square kilometres, 14% of the country, where arable land and forests suffer from climate change and poor land management. The programme plans 60 million cubic metres of small water-retaining and groundwater recharge structures on almost 700,000 hectares of forest, farmland and towns, with integrated land and water actions for each municipality, to cut runoff and floods, hold water for droughts, reduce soil erosion and cool the landscape. It builds on the 2010 to 2012 national landscape revitalisation programme and the 2005 Košice Water Protocol; it was proposed in 2018, adopted by the region in 2021 and runs to 2030. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal (2023), citing the regional plan, Kravčík and others (2012) and Sušnik and others (2022). Caveats: benefits are expected, not measured, the new water paradigm it follows is contested in parts of the hydrology literature, and monitoring results are pending. It illustrates regional adaptation planning with distributed natural water retention; a related record is the Global NbS opportunity areas dataset.
